implementation_notes: Vapor's responder chain is the front controller: types conforming to Middleware or AsyncMiddleware implement respond(to:chainingTo:) and are registered globally with app.middleware.use(_) or per group with app.grouped(_); requests traverse them in registration order and responses in reverse, with the router dispatching to route handlers at the end. What replaces the classic structure: the responder chain plus the routes collection replaces the FrontController class, and middleware registered at .beginning is inserted before Vapor's own defaults when ordering matters.
pitfalls: Middleware that must decorate error responses (CORS, for example) has to be registered at: .beginning, otherwise Vapor's ErrorMiddleware sits outside it and those responses lack the headers.
Mixing EventLoopFuture-based Middleware with AsyncMiddleware in one chain works, but blocking work in either blocks an event loop thread; offload it or use the async API.
Holding on to the Request or Response beyond the call (in a cache or task) keeps the whole context alive and leaks; per-request data belongs in the request's storage.
